summary: Assign every direct, indirect, ambient-occlusion and emissive contribution to the bake or runtime before binding a lighting-only lightmap product, with a bake-safe unwrap/channel and explicit linear-light encoding.
objective: A baked scene preserves intended static illumination without adding the same contribution again at runtime, while seams, channel selection and encoding remain inspectable.
applies_when: Static illumination is baked in Blender for a Three.js scene.
A scene mixes a lightmap with runtime lights, shadows or emissive materials.
intent_signals: avoid double lighting after a Blender bake
bind a lightmap to the intended UV channel
example_prompts: Bake indirect room lighting but keep a runtime sun without counting it twice.
Give modular walls a dedicated lightmap unwrap and verify seams and linear encoding.
negative_signals: Adding runtime copies of contributions already present in the bake.
Treating a display-ready sRGB image as linear illuminance.
not_for: Dynamic GI or moving-light shadow fidelity.
General base-color, ORM or normal-map baking.

principles: Write a contribution manifest before baking: state whether direct, indirect, AO and emission are included. Runtime may add only deliberately excluded contributions or an explicitly authored extra look.
A lightmap is illumination data. Keep its sampling UVs non-overlapping at the baked resolution, include island margin, and declare its linear-light encoding separately from display color.

Use an existing UV layout only when it is non-overlapping, sufficiently padded and stable for the bake; otherwise author a dedicated lightmap unwrap. Always bind the intended channel explicitly. The exact Three.js attribute/channel path is version dependent, so inspect the installed revision.
implementation: In Blender, choose or create a bake-safe UV set and target, record Combined contribution toggles and margin, then derive a lighting-only illuminance product appropriate for the runtime lightMap slot. Do not bind an arbitrary Combined beauty result containing material color, glossy response or visible emission and shade it again as a lightmap.
In Three.js, bind the map to the verified channel, set the documented colorSpace for the chosen file encoding, and enable only the runtime lights/shadows allowed by the contribution manifest.
Provide diagnostic toggles for lightmap-only, runtime-only and combined views; reset restores the declared combined configuration.
observable_checks: The lightmap follows the intended faces with no overlaps or mip seam bleed at the tested distance.
Lightmap-only plus runtime-only predicts the combined view; duplicated direct or indirect light is visible as a failed overbright comparison.

Before tone mapping, a neutral gray receiver and open-domain bright patch retain expected linear-light ratios after decode; then verify display output separately and record renderer revision and texture channel.

creative_affordances: Use stained light, theatrical pools or stylized baked gradients as long as ownership stays explicit.
Expose contribution toggles as a teaching or debugging view.
known_limits: A static bake cannot respond correctly to moved geometry or lights.

A full Combined or beauty bake is not automatically a valid MeshStandardMaterial lightMap; material-color, glossy and visible-emission terms require a declared conversion or different prelit presentation path.
Core glTF transport of an application lightmap binding is not asserted here.
No UV unwrap, bake, export, texture decode or render was run.

claims.statement: Blender Cycles baking requires a UV map and target and lets Combined lighting contributions including direct, indirect, AO and emission be selected; image baking can extend margins around UV islands to avoid filtering and mipmap seams.
claims.scope: Blender 4.5 Cycles bake controls; the ownership manifest is authored guidance.

claims.statement: Three.js MeshStandardMaterial documents lightMap as pre-baked illuminance, describes a second UV set, and recommends an explicit colorSpace with LinearSRGBColorSpace common for HDR lightmaps.
claims.scope: Live Three.js docs; installed UV-channel API and asset encoding must be verified.

source_refs.locator: Input color space and open-domain light-map guidance
